sections.title: What you order takes -t
sections.content: At a café the thing you order is the object, so it takes *-t*, as in *Kérek egy kávét.* The new café words follow the patterns you know: *-t* straight on after a long vowel (*kávé → kávét*), a final *-a* lengthens (*torta → tortát*), and many words ending in a consonant add a linking vowel (*fagylalt → fagylaltot*, *szendvics → szendvicset*).

sections.title: Sugar is a special case
sections.content: *Cukor* (sugar) loses its *o* before the ending: *cukor → cukrot*. Learn it as a pair: *Nem kérek cukrot.* (I do not want sugar.)

items.spanish: Kérek egy kávét és egy tortát.
items.english: I would like a coffee and a cake.

sections.content: *Kérek egy kávét* and *Kérek kávét* are both fine, but the *-t* is always there. *Kérek egy kávé* is wrong, because the coffee is what you ask for.
